notes: This contract pins Umbra's deliberately bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Request Retraction vertical slice to the exact official C++ declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. The implementation records per-recipient delivery state for normal non-regional timestamped Send Interaction, Send Interaction With Regions, Update Attribute Values (including the bounded regional path), Send Directed Interaction, and non-regional timestamped Delete Object Instance. It uses the Clause 8.22.3 strict timestamp-versus-current/requested-time-plus-actual-lookahead condition, suppresses still-queued fanout, and invokes the official callback for a recipient whose original timestamped message was already delivered. A lightweight terminal record preserves the official MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted outcome while retaining typed payload until the final pending joined recipient has crossed its callback boundary; terminal deletion state is then reclaimable. The deletion path additionally restores an execution-owned invocation snapshot—object/name/known state and committed ownership—before a legal Request Retraction callback; it does not revive or notify a departed delivered recipient. One normal-interaction case proves a live designator remains temporarily unauthorized during Disable Time Regulation and is legally retractable after callback-gated re-enable at unchanged lookahead. A second normal-interaction case restores a pre-save live record after post-save Retract terminalization, then proves the restored designator still drives the delivered recipient's Request Retraction callback. A third saves a terminal tombstone and proves it remains MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted after restore rather than aliasing a discarded post-save handle. Complete alternate-advance, broader Disable Time Regulation/re-enable, complete save/restore recovery, active in-flight ownership, other producer/recipient resignation, transport, packaging, catalog/JUnit/protected-review evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
